text: inbred lec rat: A cinnamon-colored strain of Long-Evans rats which carries a mutation causing fulminant hepatitis and jaundice, with an associated gross accumulation of copper in the liver. This strain is a model for Wilson's Disease (see HEPATOLENTICULAR DEGENERATION).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: lew rat: An inbred strain of rat that is used in BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: oletf rat: An inbred strain of Long-Evans rats that develops hyperglycemia, hyperinsulinemia, and mild obesity, mostly in males, that resembles non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus in humans. It was developed from outbred Long-Evans stock in 1983.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: shr rat: A strain of Rattus norvegicus with elevated blood pressure used as a model for studying hypertension and stroke.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: wf rat: An inbred strain of rat that is used in BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: wky rat: A strain of Rattus norvegicus used as a normotensive control for the spontaneous hypertensive rats (SHR).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Incisor: Any of the eight frontal teeth (four maxillary and four mandibular) having a sharp incisal edge for cutting food and a single root, which occurs in man both as a deciduous and a permanent tooth. (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p820)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Molar Hypomineralization: A type of developmental disturbance of AMELOGENESIS involving MOLARS of any type (obligatory) plus other teeth sometimes. It is characterized by demarcated enamel opacities with unknown systemic causation (idiopathic).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: north american indian: Members of indigenous North American populations with pre-colonial contact origins.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: south american indian: Members of indigenous South American populations with pre-colonial contact origins.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Indium Radioisotopes: Unstable isotopes of indium that decay or disintegrate emitting radiation. In atoms with atomic weights 106-112, 113m, 114, and 116-124 are radioactive indium isotopes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Infant Mortality: Postnatal deaths from BIRTH to 365 days after birth in a given population. Postneonatal mortality represents deaths between 28 days and 365 days after birth (as defined by National Center for Health Statistics). Neonatal mortality represents deaths from birth to 27 days after birth.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: neonatal intensive care: Continuous care and monitoring of newborn infants with life-threatening conditions, in any setting.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Respiratory Distress Syndrome, Newborn: A condition of the newborn marked by DYSPNEA with CYANOSIS, heralded by such prodromal signs as dilatation of the alae nasi, expiratory grunt, and retraction of the suprasternal notch or costal margins, mostly frequently occurring in premature infants, children of diabetic mothers, and infants delivered by cesarean section, and sometimes with no apparent predisposing cause.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Infectious pancreatic necrosis virus: The type species of AQUABIRNAVIRUS, causing infectious pancreatic necrosis in salmonid fish and other freshwater and marine animals including mollusks.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Injury Severity Score: An anatomic severity scale based on the Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) and developed specifically to score multiple traumatic injuries. It has been used as a predictor of mortality.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Inteins: The internal fragments of precursor proteins (INternal proTEINS) that are autocatalytically removed by PROTEIN SPLICING. The flanking fragments (EXTEINS) are ligated forming mature proteins. The nucleic acid sequences coding for inteins are considered to be MOBILE GENETIC ELEMENTS. Inteins are composed of self-splicing domains and an endonuclease domain which plays a role in the spread of the intein's genomic sequence. Mini-inteins are composed of the self-splicing domains only.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Intellectual Property: Property, such as patents, trademarks, and copyright, that results from creative effort. The Patent and Copyright Clause (Art. 1, Sec. 8, cl. 8) of the United States Constitution provides for promoting the progress of science and useful arts by securing for limited times to authors and inventors, the exclusive right to their respective writings and discoveries. (From Black's Law Dictionary, 5th ed, p1014)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: internal carotid artery: Branch of the common carotid artery which supplies the anterior part of the brain, the eye and its appendages, the forehead and nose.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: International Law: The body of law that governs the legal relations between or among sovereign states or nations.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Introns: Sequences of DNA in the genes that are located between the EXONS. They are transcribed along with the exons but are removed from the primary gene transcript by RNA SPLICING to leave mature RNA. Some introns code for separate genes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Intestinal Diseases: Pathological processes in any segment of the INTESTINE from DUODENUM to RECTUM.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Trefoil Factor-3: A 59 amino acid (6.6 kDa) trefoil factor that contains a single trefoil domain. It is expressed in all tissues with MUCOUS MEMBRANES, including GOBLET CELLS of the SMALL INTESTINE and LARGE INTESTINE. It associates with MUCIN-2 in the small intestine and may regulate epithelial CELL MIGRATION and WOUND HEALING.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Intestinal Volvulus: A twisting in the intestine (INTESTINES) that can cause INTESTINAL OBSTRUCTION.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Intestines: The section of the alimentary canal from the STOMACH to the ANAL CANAL. It includes the LARGE INTESTINE and SMALL INTESTINE.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: intravenous fat emulsion: Emulsions of fats or lipids used primarily in parenteral feeding.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Intrinsically Disordered Proteins: Functional proteins that do not have unique, stable, folded, three-dimensional native structures or that possess non-ordered regions under physiological conditions. They are characterized by extraordinary structural flexibility and plasticity, which enable them to adopt different conformations in response to different stimuli or different interactions.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Iodine Radioisotopes: Unstable isotopes of iodine that decay or disintegrate emitting radiation. I atoms with atomic weights 117-139, except I 127, are radioactive iodine isotopes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Ipomoea batatas: A plant species of the genus IPOMOEA, family CONVOLVULACEAE. Some cultivars are sweet and edible whereas bitter varieties are a source of SAPONINS. This sweet potato is sometimes referred to as a yam (DIOSCOREA).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Iridium: A metallic element with the atomic symbol Ir, atomic number 77, and atomic weight 192.22.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Iridium Radioisotopes: Unstable isotopes of iridium that decay or disintegrate emitting radiation. Ir atoms with atomic weights 182-190, 192, and 194-198 are radioactive iridium isotopes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Iridoid Glucosides: A subclass of iridoid compounds that include a glucoside moiety, usually found at the C-1 position.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Metal Workers: Craftspersons who take ordinary types of flat metal and make them into specialized products for various duct and ventilation systems, as well as architectural and specialized metal fabrication.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Iron Radioisotopes: Unstable isotopes of iron that decay or disintegrate emitting radiation. Fe atoms with atomic weights 52, 53, 55, and 59-61 are radioactive iron isotopes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Levocardia: Congenital abnormalities in which the HEART is in the normal position (levocardia) in the left side of the chest but some or all of the THORAX or ABDOMEN viscera are transposed laterally (SITUS INVERSUS). It is also known as situs inversus with levocardia, or isolated levocardia. This condition is often associated with severe heart defects and splenic abnormalities such as asplenia or polysplenia.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Pruritus: An intense itching sensation that produces the urge to rub or scratch the skin to obtain relief.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Pachysandra: A plant genus of the family BUXACEAE that should not be confused with common spurge (EUPHORBIA).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Jatropha: A plant genus of the family EUPHORBIACEAE. Members contain jatrophone and other diterpenes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia: A leukemia affecting young children characterized by SPLENOMEGALY, enlarged lymph nodes, rashes, and hemorrhages. Traditionally classed as a myeloproliferative disease, it is now considered a mixed myeloproliferative-mylelodysplastic disorder.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Karnofsky Performance Status: A performance measure for rating the ability of a person to perform usual activities, evaluating a patient's progress after a therapeutic procedure, and determining a patient's suitability for therapy. It is used most commonly in the prognosis of cancer therapy, usually after chemotherapy and customarily administered before and after therapy. It was named for Dr. David A. Karnofsky, an American specialist in cancer chemotherapy.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Shaw Potassium Channels: A shaker subfamily that is prominently expressed in NEURONS and are necessary for high-frequency, repetitive firing of ACTION POTENTIALS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Kentucky: A state bounded on the north by Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio; on the east by Virginia and west Virginia; on the south by Tennessee, and on the west by Missouri.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Parvovirus: A genus of the family PARVOVIRIDAE, subfamily PARVOVIRINAE, infecting a variety of vertebrates including humans. Parvoviruses are responsible for a number of important diseases but also can be non-pathogenic in certain hosts. The type species is MINUTE VIRUS OF MICE.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: kir receptor: A family of receptors found on NK CELLS that have specificity for a variety of HLA ANTIGENS. KIR receptors contain up to three different extracellular immunoglobulin-like domains referred to as D0, D1, and D2 and play an important role in blocking NK cell activation against cells expressing the appropriate HLA antigens thus preventing cell lysis. Although they are often referred to as being inhibitory receptors, a subset of KIR receptors may also play an activating role in NK cells.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: kir2dl5 receptor: An inhibitory KIR receptor that contains D0 and D1 extracellular immunoglobulin-like domains and a long cytoplasmic tail.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: kir3ds1 receptors: An activating KIR receptor that contains D0, D1, and D2 extracellular immunoglobulin-like domains and a short cytoplasmic tail.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: killer whale: The species Orcinus orca, in the family Delphinidae, characterized by its black and white coloration, and huge triangular dorsal fin. It is the largest member of the DOLPHINS and derives its name from the fact that it is a fearsome predator.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Norway: A country located in northern Europe, bordering the North Sea and the Atlantic Ocean, west of Sweden. The capital is Oslo.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Knee Injuries: Injuries to the knee or the knee joint.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: knockout mice: Strains of mice in which certain GENES of their GENOMES have been disrupted, or knocked-out. To produce knockouts, using RECOMBINANT DNA technology, the normal DNA sequence of the gene being studied is altered to prevent synthesis of a normal gene product. Cloned cells in which this DNA alteration is successful are then injected into mouse EMBRYOS to produce chimeric mice. The chimeric mice are then bred to yield a strain in which all the cells of the mouse contain the disrupted gene. Knockout mice are used as EXPERIMENTAL ANIMAL MODELS for diseases (DISEASE MODELS, ANIMAL) and to clarify the functions of the genes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Vulvar Lichen Sclerosus: Atrophy and shriveling of the SKIN of the VULVA that is characterized by the whitish LICHEN SCLEROSUS appearance, inflammation, and PRURITUS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Krypton Radioisotopes: Unstable isotopes of krypton that decay or disintegrate emitting radiation. Kr atoms with atomic weights 74-77, 79, 81, 85, and 87-94 are radioactive krypton isotopes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Kynurenine: A metabolite of the essential amino acid tryptophan metabolized via the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Kynurenine 3-Monooxygenase: An NADPH-dependent flavin monooxygenase that plays a key role in the catabolism of TRYPTOPHAN by catalyzing the HYDROXYLATION of KYNURENINE to 3-hydroxykynurenine. It was formerly characterized as EC 1.14.1.2 and EC 1.99.1.5.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Rats: The common name for the genus Rattus.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Laccase: A copper-containing oxidoreductase enzyme that catalyzes the oxidation of 4-benzenediol to 4-benzosemiquinone. It also has activity towards a variety of O-quinols and P-quinols. It primarily found in FUNGI and is involved in LIGNIN degradation, pigment biosynthesis and detoxification of lignin-derived products.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mammaglobin B: A MAMMAGLOBIN A-related secretoglobin that is expressed in several HUMAN tissues including the UTERUS; BREAST; SALIVARY GLAND; and LACRIMAL GLAND.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Lactation: The processes of milk secretion by the maternal MAMMARY GLANDS after PARTURITION. The proliferation of the mammary glandular tissue, milk synthesis, and milk expulsion or let down are regulated by the interactions of several hormones including ESTRADIOL; PROGESTERONE; PROLACTIN; and OXYTOCIN.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Lactoferrin: An iron-binding protein that was originally characterized as a milk protein. It is widely distributed in secretory fluids and is found in the neutrophilic granules of LEUKOCYTES. The N-terminal part of lactoferrin possesses a serine protease which functions to inactivate the TYPE III SECRETION SYSTEM used by bacteria to export virulence proteins for host cell invasion.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: large intestine: A segment of the LOWER GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT that includes the CECUM; the COLON; and the RECTUM.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: large maf transcription factors: A family of high molecular weight Maf transcription factors that contain distinct activation domains.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Maggot Debridement Therapy: Medical use of live MAGGOTS for cleaning non-healing wounds.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Lavandula: A plant genus of the LAMIACEAE family.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Law Enforcement: Organized efforts to insure obedience to the laws of a community.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Police: Agents of the law charged with the responsibility of maintaining and enforcing law and order among the citizenry.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Lead Radioisotopes: Unstable isotopes of lead that decay or disintegrate emitting radiation. Pb atoms with atomic weights 194-203, 205, and 209-214 are radioactive lead isotopes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Protein Sorting Signals: Amino acid sequences found in transported proteins that selectively guide the distribution of the proteins to specific cellular compartments.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: left ventricular function: The hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the left HEART VENTRICLE. Its measurement is an important aspect of the clinical evaluation of patients with heart disease to determine the effects of the disease on cardiac performance.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: leu cam receptor family: Family of proteins associated with the capacity of LEUKOCYTES to adhere to each other and to certain substrata, e.g., the C3bi component of complement. Members of this family are the LYMPHOCYTE FUNCTION-ASSOCIATED ANTIGEN-1; (LFA-1), the MACROPHAGE-1 ANTIGEN; (Mac-1), and the INTEGRIN ALPHAXBETA2 or p150,95 leukocyte adhesion protein. They all share a common beta-subunit which is the CD18 antigen. All three of the above antigens are absent in inherited LEUKOCYTE-ADHESION DEFICIENCY SYNDROME, which is characterized by recurrent bacterial infections, impaired pus formation, and wound healing as well as abnormalities in a wide spectrum of adherence-dependent functions of granulocytes, monocytes, and lymphoid cells.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Posterior Leukoencephalopathy Syndrome: A condition that is characterized by HEADACHE; SEIZURES; and visual loss with edema in the posterior aspects of the CEREBRAL HEMISPHERES, such as the BRAIN STEM. Generally, lesions involve the white matter (nerve fibers) but occasionally the grey matter (nerve cell bodies).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Librarians: Specialists in the management of a library or the services rendered by a library, bringing professional skills to administration, organization of material and personnel, interpretation of bibliothecal rules, the development and maintenance of the library's collection, and the provision of information services.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Lichen Sclerosus et Atrophicus: A chronic inflammatory mucocutaneous disease usually affecting the female genitalia (VULVAR LICHEN SCLEROSUS) and BALANITIS XEROTICA OBLITERANS in males. It is also called white spot disease and Csillag's disease.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Life Cycle Stages: The continuous sequence of changes undergone by living organisms during the post-embryonic developmental process, such as metamorphosis in insects and amphibians. This includes the developmental stages of apicomplexans such as the malarial parasite, PLASMODIUM FALCIPARUM.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Life Tables: Summarizing techniques used to describe the pattern of mortality and survival in populations. These methods can be applied to the study not only of death, but also of any defined endpoint such as the onset of disease or the occurrence of disease complications.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Work-Life Balance: Complex ongoing balance between a person's working life and private life.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Risk Reduction Behavior: Reduction of high-risk choices and adoption of low-risk quantity and frequency alternatives.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Photoplethysmography: Plethysmographic determination in which the intensity of light reflected from the skin surface and the red cells below is measured to determine the blood volume of the respective area. There are two types, transmission and reflectance.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Liliaceae: A monocot family within the order Liliales.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: lincrna: A class of untranslated RNA molecules that are typically greater than 200 nucleotides in length and do not code for proteins. Members of this class have been found to play roles in transcriptional regulation, post-transcriptional processing, CHROMATIN REMODELING, and in the epigenetic control of chromatin.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Semantic Web: A framework for development and promotion of common data formats and exchange protocols linked in a way that can be read directly by computers. Semantic Web is a platform for sharing and reusing data across application, enterprise, and community boundaries, by linking concepts rather than just documents.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Lipid Bilayers: Layers of lipid molecules which are two molecules thick. Bilayer systems are frequently studied as models of biological membranes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Lipogenesis: De novo fat synthesis in the body. This includes the synthetic processes of FATTY ACIDS and subsequent TRIGLYCERIDES in the LIVER and the ADIPOSE TISSUE. Lipogenesis is regulated by numerous factors, including nutritional, hormonal, and genetic elements.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Polyvinyl Alcohol: A polymer prepared from polyvinyl acetates by replacement of the acetate groups with hydroxyl groups. It is used as a pharmaceutic aid and ophthalmic lubricant as well as in the manufacture of surface coatings artificial sponges, cosmetics, and other products.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Liver-Specific Organic Anion Transporter 1: An organic anion transporter found in human and mouse liver. It is capable of transporting a variety organic anions and mediates sodium-independent uptake of bile in the liver.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

headword: Solute Carrier Organic Anion Transporter Family Member 1B3
text: Solute Carrier Organic Anion Transporter Family Member 1B3: A sodium-independent organic anion transporter that functions in the uptake of various drugs and endogenous compounds including ESTRADIOL; TAUROCHOLATE; LEUKOTRIENE C4; and METHOTREXATE. It also functions in clearing BILE ACIDS and organic anions from the liver. Mutations in the SLCO1B3 gene are associated with Rotor Type HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)
display_name: Solute Carrier Organic Anion Transporter Family Member 1B3

text: Livestock: Domesticated farm animals raised for home use or profit but excluding POULTRY. Typically livestock includes CATTLE; SHEEP; HORSES; SWINE; GOATS; and others.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Loa: A genus of parasitic nematodes found throughout the rain-forest areas of the Sudan and the basin of the Congo. L. loa inhabits the subcutaneous tissues, which it traverses freely.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Loiasis: A parasitic infection caused by the nematode Loa loa. The vector in the transmission of this infection is the horsefly (Tabanus) or the deerfly or mango fly (Chrysops). The larvae may be seen just beneath the skin or passing through the conjunctiva. Eye lesions are not uncommon. The disease is generally mild and painless.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Tabes Dorsalis: Parenchymatous NEUROSYPHILIS marked by slowly progressive degeneration of the posterior columns, posterior roots, and ganglia of the spinal cord. The condition tends to present 15 to 20 years after the initial infection and is characterized by lightening-like pains in the lower extremities, URINARY INCONTINENCE; ATAXIA; severely impaired position and vibratory sense, abnormal gait (see GAIT DISORDERS, NEUROLOGIC), OPTIC ATROPHY; Argyll-Robertson pupils, hypotonia, hyperreflexia, and trophic joint degeneration (Charcot's Joint; see ARTHROPATHY, NEUROGENIC). (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p726)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: long evans rat: An outbred strain of rats developed in 1915 by crossing several Wistar Institute white females with a wild gray male. Inbred strains have been derived from this original outbred strain, including Long-Evans cinnamon rats (RATS, INBRED LEC) and Otsuka-Long-Evans-Tokushima Fatty rats (RATS, INBRED OLETF), which are models for Wilson's disease and non-insulin dependent diabetes mellitus, respectively.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Long-Term Care: Care over an extended period, usually for a chronic condition or disability, requiring periodic, intermittent, or continuous care.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: long term care insurance: Health insurance to provide full or partial coverage for long-term home care services or for long-term nursing care provided in a residential facility such as a nursing home.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Los Angeles: City in California.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Luciferases: Enzymes that oxidize certain LUMINESCENT AGENTS to emit light (PHYSICAL LUMINESCENCE). The luciferases from different organisms have evolved differently so have different structures and substrates.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Ventilation-Perfusion Scan: A two-part radionuclide imaging that measures VENTILATION-PERFUSION RATIO of the lungs often used to investigate PULMONARY EMBOLISM. Image acquisitions may be performed using various combinations of gamma camera, PET and SPECT scanning techniques.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: RNA Methylation: The addition of a methyl group to one of the NITROGEN atoms on a NUCLEOTIDE base in an RNA molecule.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Maclura: A plant genus of the family MORACEAE. Members contain maclurin, antifungal chalcones, and other compounds.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Retinal Perforations: Perforations through the whole thickness of the retina including the macula as the result of inflammation, trauma, degeneration, etc. The concept includes retinal breaks, tears, dialyses, and holes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Oncogene Protein v-maf: An oncogene protein that was originally isolated from a spontaneous musculo-aponeurotic FIBROSARCOMA in CHICKEN and shown to be the transforming gene of the avian retrovirus AS42. It is a basic leucine zipper TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR and the founding member of the MAF TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Maf Transcription Factors: Maf transcription factors are a family of basic-leucine zipper transcription factors that are closely related to V-MAF ONCOGENE PROTEIN. The C-MAF PROTO-ONCOGENE PROTEIN was the first mammalian Maf transcription factor identified, and now the family is known to include a variety of other Maf proteins such as MAFB TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR; MAFF TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR; MAFG TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR; and MAFK TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Tinea Versicolor: A common chronic, noninflammatory and usually symptomless disorder, characterized by the occurrence of multiple macular patches of all sizes and shapes, and varying in pigmentation from fawn-colored to brown. It is seen most frequently in hot, humid, tropical regions and is mostly caused by MALASSEZIA FURFUR (formerly Pityrosporum orbiculare).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Orchiectomy: The surgical removal of one or both testicles.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: malignant pleural effusion: Presence of fluid in the PLEURAL CAVITY as a complication of malignant disease. Malignant pleural effusions often contain actual malignant cells.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Maltose: A dextrodisaccharide from malt and starch. It is used as a sweetening agent and fermentable intermediate in brewing. (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Maltose-Binding Proteins: Periplasmic proteins that bind MALTOSE and maltodextrin. They take part in the maltose transport system of BACTERIA.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mammaglobin A: A secretoglobin that is produced by the MAMMARY GLAND of HUMANS and may be involved in the binding of ANDROGENS and other STEROIDS. The expression of this protein in normal breast epithelium and in human breast cancer has made it an important histological marker.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mammals: Warm-blooded vertebrate animals belonging to the class Mammalia, including all that possess hair and suckle their young.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mandibular Condyle: The posterior process on the ramus of the mandible composed of two parts: a superior part, the articular portion, and an inferior part, the condylar neck.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mandibular Fractures: Fractures of the lower jaw.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mason-Pfizer monkey virus: A species of BETARETROVIRUS isolated from mammary carcinoma in rhesus monkeys. It appears to have evolved from a recombination between a murine B oncovirus and a primate C oncovirus related to the baboon endogenous virus. Several serologically distinct strains exist. MPMV induces SIMIAN AIDS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Masticatory Muscles: Muscles arising in the zygomatic arch that close the jaw. Their nerve supply is masseteric from the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve. (From Stedman, 25th ed)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Thalictrum: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain isoquinoline alkaloids and triterpene glycosides.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Suction: The removal of secretions, gas or fluid from hollow or tubular organs or cavities by means of a tube and a device that acts on negative pressure.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Media Exposure: The extent to which individuals encounter messages and content via COMMUNICATION MEDIA.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: medical economics: Economic aspects of the field of medicine, the medical profession, and health care. It includes the economic and financial impact of disease in general on the patient, the physician, society, or government.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Medical Record Administrators: Individuals professionally qualified in the management of patients' records. Duties may include planning, designing, and managing systems for patient administrative and clinical data, as well as patient medical records. The concept includes medical record technicians.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Medication Review: A structured evaluation of a patient‘s medicines with the aim of optimizing medicines use and improving health outcomes, detecting drug related problems and recommending interventions.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: mt2 receptor: A melatonin receptor subtype primarily found expressed in the BRAIN and RETINA.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: mt1 receptor: A melatonin receptor subtype that is primarily found in the HYPOTHALAMUS and in the KIDNEY.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: mt3 receptor: A family of G-protein-coupled receptors that are specific for and mediate the effects of MELATONIN. Activation of melatonin receptors has been associated with decreased intracellular CYCLIC AMP and increased hydrolysis of PHOSPHOINOSITIDES.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Melatonin: A biogenic amine that is found in animals and plants. In mammals, melatonin is produced by the PINEAL GLAND. Its secretion increases in darkness and decreases during exposure to light. Melatonin is implicated in the regulation of SLEEP, mood, and REPRODUCTION. Melatonin is also an effective antioxidant.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Synovial Membrane: The inner membrane of a joint capsule surrounding a freely movable joint. It is loosely attached to the external fibrous capsule and secretes SYNOVIAL FLUID.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mendelian Randomization Analysis: The use of the GENETIC VARIATION of known functions or phenotypes to correlate the causal effects of those functions or phenotypes with a disease outcome.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Psychiatric Nursing: A specialty concerned with the application of psychiatric principles in caring for the mentally ill. It also includes the nursing care provided the mentally ill patient.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mercury Radioisotopes: Unstable isotopes of mercury that decay or disintegrate emitting radiation. Hg atoms with atomic weights 185-195, 197, 203, 205, and 206 are radioactive mercury isotopes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Meristem: A group of plant cells that are capable of dividing infinitely and whose main function is the production of new growth at the growing tip of a root or stem. (From Concise Dictionary of Biology, 1990)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mesenchymal Stem Cell Transplantation: Transfer of MESENCHYMAL STEM CELLS between individuals within the same species (TRANSPLANTATION, HOMOLOGOUS) or transfer within the same individual (TRANSPLANTATION, AUTOLOGOUS).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Metabolic Reprogramming: Various cellular responses cells undergo in order to sustain energy production under cellular METABOLIC STRESS. Oncogenic metabolic reprogramming is one of the hallmarks of cancer progression and metastasis.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Methacrylates: Acrylic acids or acrylates which are substituted in the C-2 position with a methyl group.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Methylation: Addition of methyl groups. In histo-chemistry methylation is used to esterify carboxyl groups and remove sulfate groups by treating tissue sections with hot methanol in the presence of hydrochloric acid. (From Stedman, 25th ed)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Microcephaly: A congenital abnormality in which the CEREBRUM is underdeveloped, the fontanels close prematurely, and, as a result, the head is small. (Desk Reference for Neuroscience, 2nd ed.)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Microtechnology: Manufacturing technology for making microscopic devices in the micrometer range (typically 1-100 micrometers), such as integrated circuits or MEMS. The process usually involves replication and parallel fabrication of hundreds or millions of identical structures using various thin film deposition techniques and carried out in environmentally-controlled clean rooms.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Microsatellite Repeats: A variety of simple repeat sequences that are distributed throughout the GENOME. They are characterized by a short repeat unit of 2-8 basepairs that is repeated up to 100 times. They are also known as short tandem repeats (STRs).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Microsatellite Instability: The occurrence of highly polymorphic mono- and dinucleotide MICROSATELLITE REPEATS in somatic cells. It is a form of genome instability associated with defects in DNA MISMATCH REPAIR.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Middle Aged: An adult aged 45 - 64 years.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: tympanum: The space and structures directly internal to the TYMPANIC MEMBRANE and external to the inner ear (LABYRINTH). Its major components include the AUDITORY OSSICLES and the EUSTACHIAN TUBE that connects the cavity of middle ear (tympanic cavity) to the upper part of the throat.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Otitis Media with Effusion: Inflammation of the middle ear with a clear pale yellow-colored transudate.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Ossicular Prosthesis: An implant used to replace one or more of the ear ossicles. They are usually made of plastic, Gelfoam, ceramic, or stainless steel.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Otitis Media: Inflammation of the MIDDLE EAR including the AUDITORY OSSICLES and the EUSTACHIAN TUBE.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Middle Eastern and North Africans: People native to or inhabitants of the MIDDLE EAST and NORTH AFRICA.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Milk Banks: Centers for acquiring, storing, and distributing human milk.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Milk Ejection: Expulsion of milk from the mammary alveolar lumen, which is surrounded by a layer of milk-secreting EPITHELIAL CELLS and a network of myoepithelial cells. Contraction of the myoepithelial cells is regulated by neuroendocrine signals.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Milk Proteins: The major protein constituents of milk are CASEINS and whey proteins such as LACTALBUMIN and LACTOGLOBULINS. IMMUNOGLOBULINS occur in high concentrations in COLOSTRUM and in relatively lower concentrations in milk. (Singleton and Sainsbury, Dictionary of Microbiology and Molecular Biology, 2d ed, p554)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Milk Sickness: An acute, often fatal disease caused by the ingestion of milk, milk products, or the flesh of cattle or sheep which have a disease known as trembles. It is marked by weakness, anorexia, vomiting, constipation, and sometimes muscular tremors. It is caused by poisoning by white snakeroot (Eupatorium rugosum) and the rayless goldenrod (Haplopappus heterophyllus). (From Dorland, 27th ed)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Milk Substitutes: Food BEVERAGES that are used as nutritional substitutes for MILK.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Pseudocowpox Virus: A species of PARAPOXVIRUS causing a pox-like disease on udders of cows that may spread to milkers.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Self-Care Units: Rooms in health care facilities for patients who require a minimal level of care.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Minimal Clinically Important Difference: A statistically significant minimum set of clinical outcomes that demonstrates a clinical benefit of an intervention or treatment.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Minisatellite Repeats: Tandem arrays of moderately repetitive, short (10-60 bases) DNA sequences which are found dispersed throughout the GENOME, at the ends of chromosomes (TELOMERES), and clustered near telomeres. Their degree of repetition is two to several hundred at each locus. Loci number in the thousands but each locus shows a distinctive repeat unit.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: MINOCA: Myocardial infarction in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease. CORONARY CIRCULATION disruption is due to various other factors such as ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUE and CORONARY VASOSPASM.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Minority Health: The concept covering the physical and mental conditions of members of minority groups.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Synsepalum: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE. Members contain miraculin (also spelled mieraculin), a sweet protein.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mitochondrial Diseases: Diseases caused by abnormal function of the MITOCHONDRIA. They may be caused by mutations, acquired or inherited, in mitochondrial DNA or in nuclear genes that code for mitochondrial components. They may also be the result of acquired mitochondria dysfunction due to adverse effects of drugs, infections, or other environmental causes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: mitochondrial dna: Double-stranded DNA of MITOCHONDRIA. In eukaryotes, the mitochondrial GENOME is circular and codes for ribosomal RNAs, transfer RNAs, and about 10 proteins.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Uncoupling Protein 2: A mitochondrial uncoupling protein that is expressed in many tissues and exhibits the greatest expression in SKELETAL MUSCLE. It regulates mitochondrial ATP production and the generation of REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Uncoupling Protein 3: A mitochondrial uncoupling protein that is expressed in heart and skeletal muscle tissues. It functions to regulate tissue respiration, energy balance, and THERMOGENESIS. Mutations in the UCP3 gene are associated with OBESITY.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mitosis: A type of CELL NUCLEUS division by means of which the two daughter nuclei normally receive identical complements of the number of CHROMOSOMES of the somatic cells of the species.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mitosis Modulators: Agents that affect MITOSIS of CELLS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Neurofibromin 2: A membrane protein homologous to the ERM (Ezrin-Radixin-Moesin) family of cytoskeleton-associated proteins which regulate physical properties of membranes. Alterations in neurofibromin 2 are the cause of NEUROFIBROMATOSIS 2.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Monocarboxylate Transport Protein 1: A bi-directional monocarboxylic acid transporter that occurs in many different tissues, including MYOCARDIUM; LYMPHOCYTES; and MONOCYTES. It catalyzes transport across the PLASMA MEMBRANE of monocarboxylates such as LACTATE; PYRUVATE; ACETATE; and KETONE BODIES.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Morris Water Maze Test: A maze test often used to evaluate spatial learning and memory in rodent models by measuring the time it takes for a submerged platform in an open swimming arena to be found.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Theilovirus: A species of CARDIOVIRUS which contains three strains: Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis virus, Vilyuisk human encephalomyelitis virus, and Rat encephalomyelitis virus.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Tilapia: A freshwater fish used as an experimental organism and for food. This genus of the family Cichlidae (CICHLIDS) inhabits Central and South America (one species extends north into Texas), West Indies, Africa, Madagascar, Syria, and coastal India.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: SOS1 Protein: A mammalian homolog of the DROSOPHILA SON OF SEVENLESS PROTEIN. It is a guanine nucleotide exchange factor for RAS PROTEINS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Mucus: The viscous secretion of mucous membranes. It contains mucin, white blood cells, water, inorganic salts, and exfoliated cells.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Munc18 Proteins: A family of proteins involved in intracellular membrane trafficking. They interact with SYNTAXINS and play important roles in vesicular docking and fusion during EXOCYTOSIS. Their name derives from the fact that they are related to Unc-18 protein, C elegans.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Muscle Strength Dynamometer: A device that measures MUSCLE STRENGTH during muscle contraction, such as gripping, pushing, and pulling. It is used to evaluate the health status of muscle in sports medicine or physical therapy.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Sucrase: Digestive enzyme secreted in the INTESTINES. It catalyzes hydrolysis of SUCROSE to FRUCTOSE and GLUCOSE.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: mutant strains rat: Rats bearing mutant genes which are phenotypically expressed in the animals.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Myocardial Depressant Factor: A low molecular weight peptide of about 800-1000 having a negative inotropic effect. It is released into the circulation during experimental hemorrhagic pancreatitis, severe ischemia, and postoligemic shock.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Myocardial Perfusion Imaging: The creation and display of functional images showing where the blood is flowing into the MYOCARDIUM by following over time the distribution of tracers injected into the blood stream.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Myoglobin: A conjugated protein which is the oxygen-transporting pigment of muscle. It is made up of one globin polypeptide chain and one heme group.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Myrtus: A plant genus of the family MYRTACEAE. Members contain PHYTOHEMAGGLUTININS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: n3 oil: A group of unsaturated fatty acids occurring mainly in fish oils, with three double bonds at particular positions in the hydrocarbon chain.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: N-Methylaspartate: An amino acid that, as the D-isomer, is the defining agonist for the NMDA receptor subtype of glutamate receptors (RECEPTORS, NMDA).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Solute Carrier Family 12, Member 3: Na-Cl cotransporter in the convoluted segments of the DISTAL KIDNEY TUBULE. It mediates active reabsorption of sodium and chloride and is inhibited by THIAZIDE DIURETICS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Sodium-Potassium-Chloride Symporters: A subclass of symporters that specifically transport SODIUM; POTASSIUM and CHLORIDE ions across cellular membranes in a tightly coupled electroneutrality process.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Sodium-Hydrogen Exchanger 1: A sodium-hydrogen antiporter expressed by many cell types, especially on the basolateral surfaces of EPITHELIAL CELLS. It functions through an inward sodium ion chemical gradient to eliminate acids (protons) generated by metabolism and regulate intracellular pH. It is highly sensitive to AMILORIDE.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Sodium-Hydrogen Exchanger 3: A sodium-hydrogen antiporter expressed primarily by EPITHELIAL CELLS in the kidneys, it localizes to the apical membrane of the PROXIMAL KIDNEY TUBULE, where it functions in sodium and water reabsorption and possibly calcium homeostasis. It also is expressed in heart, brain, and lung tissues and is resistant to AMILORIDE inhibition.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Sodium-Hydrogen Exchangers: A family of plasma membrane exchange glycoprotein antiporters that transport sodium ions and protons across lipid bilayers. They have critical functions in intracellular pH regulation, cell volume regulation, and cellular response to many different hormones and mitogens.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Sodium Sulfate Cotransporter: A multi-pass protein that consists of 13 transmembrane helices. It is expressed primarily by renal epithelial cells and functions as a co-transporter of sodium and sulfate, to mediate sulfate reabsorption in the kidney.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Namibia: A republic in southern Africa, south of ANGOLA and west of BOTSWANA. Its capital is Windhoek.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nanovaccines: Vaccines that use NANOPARTICLES as carriers and IMMUNOLOGIC ADJUVANTS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Proprotein Convertase 9: A proprotein convertase that is essential for CHOLESTEROL homeostasis. It binds to and is required for the lysosomal degradation of the LDL RECEPTOR (LDLR); the VLDL receptor, and the APOLIPOPROTEIN E RECEPTOR. It also regulates neuronal APOPTOSIS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nasal Cavity: The proximal portion of the respiratory passages on either side of the NASAL SEPTUM. Nasal cavities, extending from the nares to the NASOPHARYNX, are lined with ciliated NASAL MUCOSA.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

headword: National Center for Health Care Technology, U.S.
text: National Center for Health Care Technology, U.S.: A center in the PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICE which coordinates and administers a program of research, demonstrations, and evaluations of medical technologies and assessments of health care technology.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)
display_name: National Center for Health Care Technology, U.S.

headword: National Health Planning Information Center, U.S.
text: National Health Planning Information Center, U.S.: A center in the HEALTH RESOURCES ADMINISTRATION Division of Planning Methods and Technology which provides access to current information on health planning and resources development.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)
display_name: National Health Planning Information Center, U.S.

text: Security Measures: Regulations to assure protection of property and equipment.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Natural Family Planning Methods: A class of natural contraceptive methods in which SEXUAL ABSTINENCE is practiced a few days before and after the estimated day of ovulation, during the fertile phase. Methods for determining the fertile period or OVULATION DETECTION are based on various physiological indicators, such as circulating hormones, changes in cervical mucus (CERVIX MUCUS), and the basal body temperature.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Natural History: A former branch of knowledge embracing the study, description, and classification of natural objects (as animals, plants, and minerals) and thus including the modern sciences of zoology, botany, and mineralogy insofar as they existed at that time. In the 17th, 18th, and 19th centuries it was much used for the generalized pursuit of certain areas of science. (Webster, 3d ed; from Dr. James H. Cassedy, NLM History of Medicine Division)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Natural Language Processing: Computer processing of a language with rules that reflect and describe current usage rather than prescribed usage.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Natural Resistance-associated Macrophage Protein 1: A cation transport protein that shares structural homology with prokaryotic and eukaryotic transport proteins. In mammals, it is a MACROPHAGE-specific antiporter, transporting metal ions in either direction against a proton gradient, and localizes to membranes of late ENDOSOMES and LYSOSOMES, where it may contribute to antimicrobial activity.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nuclear Receptor Coactivator 1: A nuclear receptor coactivator with specificity for ESTROGEN RECEPTORS; PROGESTERONE RECEPTORS; and THYROID HORMONE RECEPTORS. It contains a HISTONE ACETYLTRANSFRASE activity that may play a role in the transcriptional activation of CHROMATIN regions.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Necator americanus: A common parasite of humans in the moist tropics and subtropics. These organisms attach to villi in the small intestine and suck blood causing diarrhea, anorexia, and anemia.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Neglected Diseases: Diseases that are underfunded and have low name recognition but are major burdens in less developed countries. Neglected diseases include many tropical infectious diseases, e.g., HELMINTHIASIS; LEPROSY; LYMPHATIC FILARIASIS; ONCHOCERCIASIS; SCHISTOSOMIASIS; and TRACHOMA.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: NIMA-Related Kinases: A highly conserved family of protein serine-threonine kinases that regulate the CELL CYCLE; MITOSIS; and the response to DNA DAMAGE. They are also involved in the assembly and function of microtubule-based structures such as CILIA and CENTRIOLES.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: NIMA-Related Kinase 1: A NIMA-related kinase that functions in CELL CYCLE regulation, the control of CILIA assembly, and CENTROSOME duplication. It is activated at G2 PHASE CELL CYCLE CHECKPOINTS in response to DNA DAMAGE.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: newborn icu: Hospital units providing continuing surveillance and care to acutely ill newborn infants.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Non-Erosive Reflux Disease: A type of gastroesophageal reflux disease with acid reflux-related symptoms, but that does not affect the integrity of the ESOPHAGEAL MUCOSA.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Neurotrophin 3: A neurotrophic factor involved in regulating the survival of visceral and proprioceptive sensory neurons. It is closely homologous to nerve growth factor beta and BRAIN-DERIVED NEUROTROPHIC FACTOR.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: ngf receptors: Cell surface receptors that bind NERVE GROWTH FACTOR; (NGF) and a NGF-related family of neurotrophic factors that includes neurotrophins, BRAIN-DERIVED NEUROTROPHIC FACTOR and CILIARY NEUROTROPHIC FACTOR.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nerve Growth Factors: Factors which enhance the growth potentialities of sensory and sympathetic nerve cells.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

headword: S100 Calcium Binding Protein beta Subunit
text: S100 Calcium Binding Protein beta Subunit: A calcium-binding protein that is 92 AA long, contains 2 EF-hand domains, and is concentrated mainly in GLIAL CELLS. Elevation of S100B levels in brain tissue correlates with a role in neurological disorders.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)
display_name: S100 Calcium Binding Protein beta Subunit

text: Nuclear Export Signals: Specific amino acid sequences present in the primary amino acid sequence of proteins which mediate their export from the CELL NUCLEUS. They are rich in hydrophobic residues, such as LEUCINE and ISOLEUCINE.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Netrins: A family of extracellular proteins that are related structurally to LAMININ. They function as CHEMOTACTIC FACTORS for CELL MIGRATION and AXON GUIDANCE, acting as chemoattractants for some cell types, and as chemorepellents for others.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Netrin-1: A netrin that binds the DCC RECEPTOR or UNC5 receptors, resulting respectively in axon attraction or repulsion. Its interaction with these receptors also prevents APOPTOSIS; it may function as a tumor suppressor protein.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Netrin Receptors: Cell surface receptors that bind NETRINS. They typically contain both IMMUNOGLOBULIN DOMAINS and FIBRONECTIN TYPE III DOMAINS and function to mediate CELL MIGRATION and AXON GUIDANCE.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Neural Tube: A tube of ectodermal tissue in an embryo that will give rise to the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM, including the SPINAL CORD and the BRAIN. Lumen within the neural tube is called neural canal which gives rise to the central canal of the spinal cord and the ventricles of the brain. For malformation of the neural tube, see NEURAL TUBE DEFECTS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Proprotein Convertase 1: A CALCIUM-dependent endopeptidase that has specificity for cleavage at ARGININE that is near paired basic residues. It cleaves a variety of prohormones including PRO-OPIOMELANOCORTIN; PRORENIN; proenkephalins; prodynorphin; prosomatostatin; and PROINSULIN.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: nf1 gene: Tumor suppressor genes located on the long arm of human chromosome 17 in the region 17q11.2. Mutation of these genes is thought to cause NEUROFIBROMATOSIS 1, Watson syndrome, and LEOPARD syndrome.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: nf2 gene: Tumor suppressor genes located on the long arm of human chromosome 22. Mutation or loss of these genes causes NEUROFIBROMATOSIS 2.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Neurofibromin 1: A protein found most abundantly in the nervous system. Defects or deficiencies in this protein are associated with NEUROFIBROMATOSIS 1, Watson syndrome, and LEOPARD syndrome. Mutations in the gene (GENE, NEUROFIBROMATOSIS 1) affect two known functions: regulation of ras-GTPase and tumor suppression.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: nk 1 receptor: A class of cell surface receptors for TACHYKININS with a preference for SUBSTANCE P. Neurokinin-1 (NK-1) receptors have been cloned and are members of the G protein coupled receptor superfamily. They are found on many cell types including central and peripheral neurons, smooth muscle cells, acinar cells, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and immune cells.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Neurokinin-1 Receptor Antagonists: Compounds that inhibit or block the activity of NEUROKININ-1 RECEPTORS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Neurologists: Qualified medical professionals who specialize in treating NERVOUS SYSTEM DISEASES.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Norepinephrine Plasma Membrane Transport Proteins: Sodium chloride-dependent neurotransmitter symporters located primarily on the PLASMA MEMBRANE of noradrenergic neurons. They remove NOREPINEPHRINE from the EXTRACELLULAR SPACE by high affinity reuptake into PRESYNAPTIC TERMINALS. The norepinephrine transporter regulates signal amplitude and duration at noradrenergic synapses and is the target of ADRENERGIC UPTAKE INHIBITORS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Neuroprotective Agents: Drugs intended to prevent damage to the brain or spinal cord from ischemia, stroke, convulsions, or trauma. Some must be administered before the event, but others may be effective for some time after. They act by a variety of mechanisms, but often directly or indirectly minimize the damage produced by endogenous excitatory amino acids.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: trkc protein: A protein-tyrosine kinase receptor that is specific for NEUROTROPHIN 3. It is widely expressed in nervous tissue and may play a role in mediating the effects of NEUROTROPHIN 3 on the proliferation and differentiation of NEURONS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: neutralizing antibody: Antibodies that reduce or abolish some biological activity of a soluble antigen or infectious agent, usually a virus.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Neutropenia: A decrease in the number of NEUTROPHILS found in the blood.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: New South Wales: A state in southeastern Australia. Its capital is Sydney. It was discovered by Captain Cook in 1770 and first settled at Botany Bay by marines and convicts in 1788. It was named by Captain Cook who thought its coastline resembled that of South Wales. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p840 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p377)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Tobacco Use Disorder: Tobacco used to the detriment of a person's health or social functioning. Tobacco dependence is included.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Tobacco Use Cessation Devices: Devices or delivery systems used to aid in ending a TOBACCO habit.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nippostrongylus: A genus of intestinal nematode parasites belonging to the superfamily HELIGMOSOMATOIDEA, which commonly occurs in rats but has been experimentally transmitted to other rodents and rabbits. Infection is usually through the skin.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nitrogen Radioisotopes: Unstable isotopes of nitrogen that decay or disintegrate emitting radiation. N atoms with atomic weights 12, 13, 16, 17, and 18 are radioactive nitrogen isotopes.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nuclear Localization Signals: Short, predominantly basic amino acid sequences identified as nuclear import signals for some proteins. These sequences are believed to interact with specific receptors at the NUCLEAR PORE.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Noncommunicable Diseases: Diseases which are typically non-infectious in origin and do not transmit from an affected individual to others. The four main types of noncommunicable diseases are CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES (e.g., heart attacks and stroke), CANCER, chronic respiratory diseases (e.g., CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE and ASTHMA) and DIABETES MELLITUS.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: nonmedical residency: Advanced programs of training to meet certain professional requirements in fields other than medicine or dentistry, e.g., pharmacology, nutrition, nursing, etc.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: nonsexual harassment: The act of systematic and/or continuous unwanted and irritating actions of a non-sexual nature, by a party or group against another. This behavior may include threats, BULLYING, taunts, blackmail, and demands.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Periodontal Debridement: Removal or disruption of DENTAL DEPOSITS and plaque-retentive DENTAL CALCULUS from tooth surfaces and within the periodontal pocket space without deliberate removal of CEMENTUM as done in ROOT PLANING and often in DENTAL SCALING. The goal is to conserve dental cementum to help maintain or re-establish healthy periodontal environment and eliminate PERIODONTITIS by using light instrumentation strokes and nonsurgical techniques (e.g., ultrasonic, laser instruments).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Northern Ireland: The northern one-sixth of the island of Ireland - between the North Atlantic Ocean and the North Sea; northwest of France. The capital is Belfast.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nuclear Envelope: The membrane system of the CELL NUCLEUS that surrounds the nucleoplasm. It consists of two concentric membranes separated by the perinuclear space. The structures of the envelope where it opens to the cytoplasm are called the nuclear pores (NUCLEAR PORE).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nuclear Matrix: The residual framework structure of the CELL NUCLEUS that maintains many of the overall architectural features of the cell nucleus including the nuclear lamina with NUCLEAR PORE complex structures, residual CELL NUCLEOLI and an extensive fibrogranular structure in the nuclear interior. (Advan. Enzyme Regul. 2002; 42:39-52)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nuclear Matrix-Associated Proteins: A broad category of nuclear proteins that are components of or participate in the formation of the NUCLEAR MATRIX.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nurse's Role: The expected function of a member of the nursing profession.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: nursing economic: Economic aspects of the nursing profession.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nursing Evaluation Research: Research carried out by nurses that uses interviews, data collection, observation, surveys, etc., to evaluate nursing, health, clinical, and nursing education programs and curricula, and which also demonstrates the value of such evaluation.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nursing Home Residents: Persons who reside in NURSING HOMES.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: nursing model: Theoretical models simulating behavior or activities in nursing, including nursing care, management and economics, theory, assessment, research, and education. Some examples of these models include Orem Self-Care Model, Roy Adaptation Model, and Rogers Life Process Model.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nut and Peanut Hypersensitivity: Allergic reaction to tree nuts and peanuts, including other LEGUMES, that is triggered by the immune system. It includes co-sensitization to other food (e.g., sesame seed).
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nutritional Sciences: The study of NUTRITION PROCESSES as well as the components of food, their actions, interaction, and balance in relation to health and disease.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nutritional Status: State of the body in relation to the consumption and utilization of nutrients.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nymphaeaceae: The water lily plant family of aquatic, rhizomatous herbs in the class Magnoliopsida.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Nyssa: A plant genus of the family Nyssaceae. Named for the water nymph from classical mythology, these species grow in moist habitats and are tolerant of flooding.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Organic Anion Transport Protein 1: A polyspecific transporter for organic cations found primarily in the kidney. It mediates the coupled exchange of alpha-ketoglutarate with organic ions such as P-AMINOHIPPURIC ACID.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Obsessive Behavior: Persistent, unwanted idea or impulse which is considered normal when it does not markedly interfere with mental processes or emotional adjustment.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: obstructive sleep apnea: A disorder characterized by recurrent apneas during sleep despite persistent respiratory efforts. It is due to upper airway obstruction. The respiratory pauses may induce HYPERCAPNIA or HYPOXIA. Cardiac arrhythmias and elevation of systemic and pulmonary arterial pressures may occur. Frequent partial arousals occur throughout sleep, resulting in relative SLEEP DEPRIVATION and daytime tiredness. Associated conditions include OBESITY; ACROMEGALY; MYXEDEMA; micrognathia; MYOTONIC DYSTROPHY; adenotonsilar dystrophy; and NEUROMUSCULAR DISEASES. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p395)
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: occupational air pollutants: Toxic air-borne matter related to work performed They are usually produced by the specific nature of the occupation.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Ocean Acidification: Reduction in OCEAN WATER overall pH. Ocean acidification is linked to CORAL BLEACHING and may disturb other marine BIODIVERSITY.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Organic Cation Transporter 1: An organic cation transporter found in kidney. It is localized to the basal lateral membrane and is likely to be involved in the renal secretion of organic cations.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Organic Cation Transporter 2: Organic cation transporter consisting of twelve transmembrane domains and expressed primarily in the kidney. It transports a wide range of metabolites, drugs, and neurotransmitters from the blood to the KIDNEY TUBULES, including DOPAMINE; SEROTONIN; CHOLINE; and CISPLATIN.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Ophthalmology: A surgical specialty concerned with the structure and function of the eye and the medical and surgical treatment of its defects and diseases.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Walruses: The family Odobenidae, suborder PINNIPEDIA, order CARNIVORA. It is represented by a single species of large, nearly hairless mammal found on Arctic shorelines, whose upper canines are modified into tusks.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

headword: United States Office of Technology Assessment
text: United States Office of Technology Assessment: An office established to help Congress participate and plan for the consequences of uses of technology. It provided information on both the beneficial and adverse effects of technological applications. The Office of Technology Assessment closed on September 29, 1995.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)
display_name: United States Office of Technology Assessment

text: Onchocerca volvulus: A species of parasitic nematodes widely distributed throughout central Africa and also found in northern South America, southern Mexico, and Guatemala. Its intermediate host and vector is the blackfly or buffalo gnat.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Oncologists: Physicians specializing in MEDICAL ONCOLOGY or its sub-specialties of RADIATION ONCOLOGY or SURGICAL ONCOLOGY.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: One Health: An integrative effort of multiple disciplines working collaboratively and locally, nationally, and globally in all aspects of health care for humans, animals, and the environment.
licence: public domain (MeSH 2026, courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine)

text: Single-Parent Family: A household that includes children and is headed by one adult parent.
